notes: Kinematic swimming reference for the paddle crab, keyframed by eye from blue crab footage. See kinematic_ref.py for the format and joint conventions.

Two gaits, each with its own paddle stroke. Clips pair up by gait: 000106 (front, slightly below) and 000014 (behind and below) show sideways swimming; 000094 (side) and 000054 (above) show paddles-first swimming.

The paddles slice continuously: each tip carves a loop (the base swing timed against the raise), and the blade angle is given relative to the tip's own motion (slice: 0 broadside, 90 edge-first), turning gradually rather than flipping.
A paddle that looks broad to a camera faces it; one that looks thin is edge-on to it.

paddles_first (both paddles point back, the far one ~0.6 of a stroke behind the near one; claws forward, centre legs down and back): power is broadside up over the back toward the head and in toward the midline (~50 deg past vertical at phase ~0.3); the blade twists edge-first as it comes back, the paddle swings out to the side and down beside the body (phase ~0.7-0.8), sweeps in behind and rises.

sideways (the robot is mirrored for 000106, whose crab swims toward its left; footage is never mirrored): the leading paddle strokes broadside up and over the back toward the trailing side, then slices back and circles near upright through the second half; the trailing paddle is held up and out ~45 deg and strokes out of phase (broadside, out and down to ~20 deg above horizontal while the leading paddle recovers, phase ~0.42-0.72), then slices back up. 000106 shows the trailing stroke ~0.15 earlier than 000014; the keys split the difference. The leading hanging leg folds up during the sweep.

History: v1 inverted broad/thin; v2 fixed it; v3 matched sweep timing; v4/v5 compared clips through mirrored footage and misread 000094; v6 unmirrored footage and added paddles_first; v7 second views (000014, 000054); v8 trailing paddle out of phase; v9 separate strokes per gait, looping tip paths and slicing blades.
